NAHHAS:v5p11/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p11/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p11/r7.claim: Subḥāna is a cognate accusative; they call themselves unjust for putting things out of their proper place by withholding what was due.

THALABI:v10p16#2/r23.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p16#2/r23.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p16#2/r23.claim: They declare God free of injustice and admit that they themselves were unjust.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p106/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p106/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p106/r1.claim: They declare God free of injustice in what He did and acknowledge their own wrongdoing in disobeying Him and withholding from the poor.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p106/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p106/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p106/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says they seek forgiveness for what they did, then blame one another for deciding to deprive the poor.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:28-34/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:28-34/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:28-34/r2.claim: They declare God free of wrongdoing and admit they wronged themselves.

JISHUMI:v10p7034/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7034/r20.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7034/r20.claim: Their declaration that God is exalted means He did not wrong them; their own injustice lay in deciding to deny the poor their due.

JISHUMI:v10p7036/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r6.claim: Their admission that they had been unjust shows injustice is an act of the servant.

JISHUMI:v10p7036/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r8.claim: After sin, a servant should turn back to God; Hasan advised against fighting al-Hajjaj with the sword and urged repentance and prayer, since God would not grant victory while people persisted in sin.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p197/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p197/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p197/r1.claim: They declare God free of injustice and admit they wronged the poor by withholding their due.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r14.claim: The brothers repented and returned to God; they had been believers from among the People of the Book.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p350/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p350/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p350/r1.claim: The brothers' words سبحان ربنا refute the claim that their earlier تسبيح meant saying an exception; they repent, glorify God, and admit their wrongful intent to bar the poor.

TABRISI:68:17-33/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:17-33/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:17-33/r19.claim: They admitted wrongdoing in planning to deprive the poor; God is above injustice, so their loss was their own fault, not a wrong done to them.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p338#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p338#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p338#4/r1.claim: They declared God free of injustice and admitted their own injustice in denying the poor.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:28-32/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:28-32/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:68:28-32/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says their declaration of God’s glory means they sought forgiveness for their sin; they admit they wronged themselves by denying the poor.

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:27-32/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:27-32/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:27-32/r3.claim: They praised God and admitted wrongdoing: the reminder may mean they should have said God willing, called glorification because both exalt God, or because nothing occurs in His dominion against His will.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#9/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#9/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#9/r1.claim: After the orchard was ruined, they finally said what they had been urged to say beforehand, admitted injustice in withholding charity and failing to make an exception, and declared God free of injustice.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that after rebuke they returned to God's remembrance, acknowledged wrongdoing, and asked forgiveness.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r8.claim: They praise God and confess their injustice too late; they blame one another for withholding the poor’s share, admit transgression, and hope God replaces the garden, perhaps in this life or as a reward in the next.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r9.claim: Some early scholars say the brothers lived in Yemen near Sana’a or in Abyssinia; their righteous father maintained the garden, kept a year’s provisions, and gave the surplus to the poor, but his sons called this foolish and were punished by losing crop, profit, and charity.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p106/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p106/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p106/r6.claim: They immediately repent, declaring God free of injustice and confessing entrenched wrongdoing: they withheld their father's charity and swore without referring the outcome to God.

BURSEVI:v10p89/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p89/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p89/r1.claim: They admit they wronged the poor by intending to withhold their due out of stinginess.

BURSEVI:v10p89/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p89/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p89/r2.claim: Their confession is repentance for corrupt intent; they would have escaped punishment had they spoken before the calamity, but spoke after the garden was ruined.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r1.claim: Their tasbih recalls God, and their confession of wrongdoing expresses regret and repentance, though it came after the sin.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r2.claim: A second interpretation takes tasbih as an exception equivalent to saying inshaAllah, because both exception and glorification entrust matters to and exalt God.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r3.speaker: السدي وابن جريج ومجاهد وأبو صالح
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r3.claim: They report that in their time tasbih served as the expression for an exception, like our saying inshaAllah.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r4.speaker: بعض الحنفية
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r4.claim: Some Hanafi jurists treat سبحان الله as a valid present-day exception in a divorce formula, so the divorce would not take effect.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r5.speaker: ابن الهمام
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r5.claim: The ruling was attributed to Ibn al-Humam and his legal opinions, but some later scholars denied both the attribution and the existence of those opinions.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r6.speaker: النحاس
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r6.claim: Al-Nahhas's rationale is preferable: saying سبحان الله declares God above anything occurring except by His will.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r7.claim: Another possibility is that the interpretation relies on a true transmitted practice and the principle that earlier revealed law applies when recounted without disapproval.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#4/r8.claim: A further gloss takes the phrase to mean that they should seek forgiveness.

ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r19.claim: They exalt God and admit that their thoughtless oath, omission of an exception, and resolve to neglect the poor wronged themselves.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p86/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p86/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p86/r6.claim: Their reply acknowledges that he had warned them and they disobeyed; their glorification recognizes that they violated God's command to give the poor their due.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p86/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p86/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p86/r7.claim: Repentance begins with acknowledging harm to the poor and restoring what can be restored; glorifying God precedes asking forgiveness, as in 110:3.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p87/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p87/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p87/r1.claim: إنا كنا ظالمين confesses guilt; إن emphasizes the admission and explains the preceding glorification, while the omitted object covers harm to themselves and to the poor.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p87/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p87/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p87/r2.claim: The uncoordinated answer follows conversational narration, as in the cited exchange in the second chapter.

TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas tells of a father who always gave each rightful person a share, then five sons who planned to keep an unusually abundant harvest from Muslim poor; four agreed and the moderate brother objected.

TABATABAI:68:29-33/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:29-33/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:29-33/r2.claim: Their declaration that God is transcendent repudiates the partners they implicitly asserted in their oath and confesses that they wronged themselves; on the other reading it also repents of wronging the poor.

BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.claim: Exegetes elaborate the garden story: it belonged to a righteous man who left it to his people and town; reports place it in Yemen near Ṣanʿāʾ, Abyssinia, or among the People of Scripture.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p434/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p434/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p434/r4.claim: Their immediate confession acknowledges that success had intoxicated them, making them forget God’s majesty and ignore reminders.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p434/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p434/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p434/r5.claim: Their confession parallels Pharaoh’s at the point of drowning; repentance after its proper time is futile.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r9.claim: The brothers ignored the sensible sibling's warning, recognized his correctness after seeing the destroyed garden, repented, and regretted their actions, but too late.

STUDYQURAN:68:17/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r15.claim: They were wrongdoers because they prevented the poor from receiving their due.
